extracted.intended_audience: patentees, patent practitioners, fee submitters, and USPTO maintenance-fee processors
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive rules for submitting, verifying, and resolving maintenance fee payments and related documentation for U.S. patents before the USPTO, including entity-status assertions, payment methods, identification requirements, and remedies for late/insufficient payments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grouping and ordering multiple-patent payments
rubrics_metrics.description: If maintenance fee payments for more than one patent are submitted together, they should be submitted on as few sheets as possible with the patent numbers listed in increasing patent number order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the payment submitted is insufficient to cover the maintenance fees and surcharges for all the listed patents, the payment will be applied in the order the patents are listed, beginning at the top of the listing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of loss of small (or micro) entity status timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of any change in status resulting in loss of entitlement to small entity status must be filed in a patent prior to paying, or at the time of paying, the earliest maintenance fee due after the date on which status as a small entity is no longer appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Similar requirement and timing apply for loss of micro entity status; filings must comply with 37 CFR 1.27(g) and 1.29(i).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund limitations for maintenance fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees and surcharges relating thereto will not be refunded except in accordance with 37 CFR 1.26 and 1.28(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A patentee cannot obtain a refund of a maintenance fee that was due and payable on the patent. Any duplicate payment will be refunded to the fee submitter. See MPEP §§ referenced for procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may pay and fee-address consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: The patentee may pay maintenance fees and any necessary surcharges or any person or organization may pay maintenance fees and any necessary surcharges on behalf of the patentee without filing evidence of authorization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No verification of authority will be made by the Office. If payment is accepted, notices relating to maintenance fees will be mailed to the 'fee address' set forth in 37 CFR 1.363. If payment is not accepted, it will be returned to the submitter if a return address is available. It is strongly recommended the payor include a return address and telephone number to assist Office contact and identification (see MPEP § 2530).

rubrics_metrics.name: Amount and timing requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: A maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge for a patent must be submitted in the amount due on the date the maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge are paid, and at the proper time, i.e., within the periods set forth in 37 CFR 1.362.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the amount of the maintenance fee is correct on the date it is paid and credited to the patent, a later change in the maintenance fees will not require modification of the amount paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required identification: patent and application numbers
rubrics_metrics.description: A maintenance fee payment must include the patent number and the application number on which the maintenance fee is being paid (37 CFR 1.366(c)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the payment includes only the patent number, the Office may apply the payment to the patent identified or may return it. The application number required is the application that matured into the patent; for reissue patents use the reissue application number. See MPEP § 2530 for special acceptance guidance and possible petitions under 1.377/1.378 if identifying data was not present.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedies for expired patents due to nonpayment
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent expires because the maintenance fee and any necessary surcharge have not been paid in the manner required, the patentee could proceed under 37 CFR 1.378 or file a petition under 37 CFR 1.377 within the periods set therein seeking acceptance of the maintenance fee.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See MPEP §§ 2580 (1.377) and 2590 (1.378) for petition practice and requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional but recommended submission details (1.366(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: Under 37 CFR 1.366(d), the following information should also be submitted for each patent on which a maintenance fee or surcharge is paid: (A) the fee year (3 1/2, 7 1/2, or 11 1/2 year fee); (B) the amount of the maintenance fee and any surcharge being submitted; (C) any assigned customer number; and (D) whether entity status is being changed or claimed with the payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This information is not mandatory but would expedite processing. For reissue patents, furnish the original patent number in addition to the requested information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Maintenance Fee Transmittal Form PTO/SB/45
rubrics_metrics.description: The Maintenance Fee Transmittal Form, PTO/SB/45 should be used when submitting maintenance fees by mail or by facsimile transmission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Form is available from the Maintenance Fee Branch and the USPTO website (www.uspto.gov/patent/patents-forms#patent).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing order for submitted fees
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office processes fees in the order in which they are presented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a single payment is insufficient to cover multiple listed patents and there is no general authorization to charge a deposit account, the payment will be applied in the order the patents are listed (increasing patent number order is recommended).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee amounts, CPI adjustments, and entity reductions
rubrics_metrics.description: 37 CFR 1.20(e)-(h) sets the fee amounts for maintenance fees and the grace period surcharge; maintenance fee amounts are subject to CPI adjustment pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 41(f).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintenance fee amounts are subject to a 60% reduction for small entities (35 U.S.C. 41(h)) and an 80% reduction for micro entities. The Maintenance Fee Branch or USPTO Fee Information website provides current amounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: No proration for shortened patent term
rubrics_metrics.description: If the term of a patent is shortened (e.g., by a terminal disclaimer) so that it will expire part way between due dates, the entire maintenance fee amount for the due date must still be paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The maintenance fee amount cannot be prorated to cover only the portion of time before the patent expires.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted payment methods and negotiability
rubrics_metrics.description: The payment shall be made in U.S. dollars and in the form of a cashier’s or certified check, Treasury note, national bank notes, or United States Postal Service money order as provided in 37 CFR 1.23(a).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If sent in another form the Office may delay or cancel the credit until collection is made. Personal or uncertified checks that are not immediately negotiable (e.g., lack signature or insufficient funds) will not constitute payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Credit card payments and security
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees can be charged to a credit card as set forth in 37 CFR 1.23(b), but credit for the payment is subject to actual receipt by the Office.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Credit Card Payment Form (PTO-2038) unless payment is over the internet. If credit card information is provided on other forms/documents, the Office will not be liable if the number becomes public knowledge. See MPEP § 509.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign remittances requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any remittance from a foreign country must be payable and immediately negotiable in the United States for the full amount of the maintenance fee and/or surcharge required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure foreign instruments meet U.S. negotiability standards to avoid processing delays or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorization to charge deposit account rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fees and surcharges may be paid by authorization to charge a deposit account established pursuant to 37 CFR 1.25, but the authorization must be submitted within an appropriate window and must be limited to fees payable on the date of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorization cannot be submitted prior to the 3 1/2, 7 1/2, or 11 1/2 year fee windows; it must permit immediate charging (not deferred). An authorization that only authorizes charging at a later date will not constitute payment. Any insufficient authorization/funds will not constitute payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separate submission of maintenance fees (no commingling)
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fee payments and any surcharges relating thereto must be submitted separately from any other payments for fees or charges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commingled payments (e.g., with filing fees, issue fees, document supply fees) will not be accepted since maintenance fees are processed by a separate area of the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special acceptance scenarios for informalities (I-III)
rubrics_metrics.description: Under MPEP § 2530, the Office may specially accept payments with certain informalities: I) patent number supplied but no application number; II) both numbers supplied but they do not correspond; III) no patent number supplied but application number supplied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: I: Office may apply payment to patent identified or return it. II: Office will generally apply payment to patent identified by patent number if possible, but may return or apply to corroborated patent based on additional info. III: Office may apply payment if corroborating information is present or may return it. A Notice of Special Acceptance (PTO-2143) will be mailed identifying what patent the fee was applied to and asking submitter to verify; timely petition may be required if misapplied.

rubrics_metrics.name: When payment is late or insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples of late or insufficient payments include: (A) payment received but additional funds required due to surcharge or fee increase; (B) payment received in small-entity amount but no assertion of small entity status in file; (C) payment received after the patent expired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If payment considered late or insufficient, a Notice of Non-Acceptance (PTO-2142) will be sent to the fee submitter; reply is required prior to expiration of the grace period under 37 CFR 1.362(e) to avoid expiration. If reply not timely, a petition under 1.377 or 1.378 is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplicate payment handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a duplicate payment is submitted for a patent already paid by a first fee submitter, the Office intends to treat the duplicate payment as follows depending on whether it complies with 37 CFR 1.366(c).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A: If duplicate lacks both patent and application numbers, Office will return it to second submitter with indication patent already paid. B: If duplicate contains both numbers, Office will verify first payment. (1) If first payment properly processed, return duplicate to second submitter with identification of first submitter. (2) If first payment not properly processed, Office will attempt to apply the duplicate (and retract first payment) or return the duplicate with identification of first submitter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee address for maintenance fee communications
rubrics_metrics.description: All notices, receipts, refunds, and other communications relating to payment or refund of maintenance fees will be directed to the correspondence address used during prosecution unless a fee address for maintenance fee purposes is set forth when submitting the issue fee or later designated (37 CFR 1.363).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A fee address must be an address associated with a Customer Number. Use Fee Address Indication Form (PTO/SB/47) and Request for Customer Number (PTO/SB/125) if necessary. Designate fee address prior to or at time of payment to ensure proper routing. Assignment does not change fee/correspondence address automatically.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office has no duty to notify patentees of due fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Under statutes and regulations, the Office has no duty to notify patentees when their maintenance fees are due; it is solely the responsibility of the patentee to ensure timely payment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will attempt to assist by mailing a Maintenance Fee Reminder during the grace period, but reminders are courtesies and errors or failure to receive them do not relieve the patentee of the obligation. See relevant case law (Rydeen v. Quigg) cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claiming small or micro entity discounts (timing and form)
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish small entity status for paying a maintenance fee, a written assertion must be filed prior to or with the maintenance fee paid as a small entity; for micro entity status, a written certification must be filed prior to or at the time the maintenance fee is paid in the micro entity amount.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A written assertion of small entity status need only be filed once and remains effective until changed. Certifications must be signed by authorized person per 37 CFR 1.33(b). Refund provisions of 37 CFR 1.28(a) apply to later small entity assertions, but later-submitted micro entity certifications are not refundable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification and form for removal of entity status
rubrics_metrics.description: Notification of any change resulting in loss of entitlement to an entity status must be filed in a patent prior to paying, or at the time of paying, the earliest maintenance fee due after the date on which status is no longer appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 37 CFR 1.27(g)(2) requires loss of small entity status to be a specific written notification (see MPEP § 509.03(b)). Form SB/460 may be used for loss of micro entity status. All notifications must be signed by a party identified in 37 CFR 1.33(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling payments that conflict with entity-status record (Overpayment/Underpayment notices)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a payment conflicts with the Office record of the patentee’s entity status, the Office will send an Overpayment Notice (if Office record indicates a reduction that would lower the submitted amount) or an Underpayment Notice (if Office record indicates no entitlement to the discounted amount submitted).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A non-extendable ONE MONTH period from mailing date of notice is provided for filing notification of loss of entitlement; however, if additional money is required, the reply (including additional money and any entitlement notice) must be filed within the earlier of that one-month period or any remaining time under 37 CFR 1.362 (including grace period). Absent a timely reply to Overpayment, Office will apply reduced amount and refund overpayment; absent timely reply to Underpayment, Office will return amount received. If payment returned and no time remains in grace period, a petition under 1.378 must be filed to seek acceptance of an unintentionally delayed payment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance fee payment status inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Maintenance fee payment status information for a patent can be obtained over the internet by entering the patent number and corresponding application number at https://fees.uspto.gov/MaintenanceFees or by telephone (limited to two patent numbers per call).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contact Maintenance Fee Branch or see MPEP § 1730 for telephone number; forms and online storefront have limitations (e.g., cannot accept entity-status documents).

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing and notice of special acceptance (PTO-2143) and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office specially accepts a payment under scenarios I–III, it will mail a Notice of Special Acceptance of Patent Maintenance Fee (PTO-2143) to the submitter identifying the patent and application to which the maintenance fee was applied and requesting verification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the payment was not applied as intended, a petition (e.g., under 37 CFR 1.377) must be filed. If not filed within 2 months of the notice date, the petition may be dismissed as untimely and relief may need to be pursued under 37 CFR 1.378(a)-(c).
